speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what happens when you wake up frightened? Do you seem fully awake and remember the dream, or do you appear confused and unable to be comforted?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: She is able to be consoled and does not appear confused, which suggests nightmares rather than sleep terrors. Does she remember the content of the frightening dreams when she wakes up?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying that she remembers the bad dreams. To rule out other causes, has she experienced any recent stressors, changes in routine, or exposure to frightening media? Also, does she snore or have pauses in breathing during sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text:
She recalls the dreams and can be consoled, which strongly points toward Nightmare Disorder rather than sleep terrors. I will now confirm the final diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder
